_comment: SINGLE canonical qualifying-receipt predicate. All consumers (Rust validate_status.rs + history_queries.rs via assess, Python query.py + publish_receipt.py, bash/jq verify_receipt.sh) MUST read this file instead of an inline copy, so tightening the floor is ONE edit here. Colocated with rebase-base-floors.json / gate_floors.py. Drift resolutions per task one-shared-qualifying-receipt-predicate-five-consumers-bypass-the-registry (design note 2026-08-04 18:17); source sweep ai_docs/2026-08-04-floor-consumer-sweep.md.
_completeness_is_coverage_not_count: For a count-capable receipt (schema_version >= counts_schema) COMPLETENESS is decided by per-node COVERAGE (planned_test_nodes > 0 AND no zero_executed_nodes AND no absent_nodes), NOT by the executed_tests COUNT. executed_tests is a proxy in BOTH directions (landed dev-hermit d05874e; proof ee303899: 8 PASS rows at executed=427 but coverage 4/19 planned nodes, 15 absent -> legitimately NOT full green). executed_tests_min below is ONLY the surviving zero-execution floor (a run that executed nothing is never green), never a completeness discriminator; old-schema receipts that predate coverage fall back to it because it is the strongest thing they can prove.
_accepts_green_class: WHICH GREEN CLASS MAY LAND. hard = validation executed at THIS exact head. soft-* = inherited from an ancestor head and speculatively trusted (the row carries validated_head_sha != commit plus an inherited_from provenance block). Defaulting to [hard] keeps today's behaviour EXACTLY -- measured: all 585 live ledger rows classify hard, because a row with no validated_head_sha derives it as commit. What changes is that the acceptance is now STATED rather than implied by the absence of a soft producer. Derivation + refusals live in ci-hub/validate/green_class.py; consumers must not restate them. NOTE: the Rust readers ignore unknown predicate keys (no deny_unknown_fields), so this clause is enforced by the PYTHON consumer only until lib/qualifying_receipt.rs reads it -- see ai_docs/fix-inert-determinism-parity-guards-20260806.md.
